subject: Deployment boundary & end-to-end traffic flow for private VPC
messages:
From: Sarah Murphy <sarah.murphy@heliosfi.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial: private VPC boundary & e2e traffic flow

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this on. We're kicking off a private deployment evaluation and need to validate the control-plane / data-plane split and what traffic needs to cross our boundary. High level asks:

- Confirm whether Redwood requires inbound connectivity to customer networks or if an outbound-only model (customer -> Redwood endpoints) is sufficient.
- Who terminates TLS (customer edge vs Redwood proxy) and where key material must reside for SOC2 proofing.
- Audit log requirements and whether runtime telemetry (token-level usage) can be restricted to the control plane in the Redwood VPC.
- Example diagrams showing the demarcation point, egress whitelist, and reference HA patterns.

We're aiming for a short workshop next week with architecture and security stakeholders. Attached is a quick network map from our infra team.

Attachments: customer-netmap-hel-20261212.pdf (see inline)

Thanks,
Sarah Murphy
Sr. Cloud Architect | Helios Financial Services
smurphy@heliosfi.com
+1 (415) 555-0148
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Murphy <sarah.murphy@heliosfi.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial: private VPC boundary & e2e traffic flow

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front: an outbound-only model is supported and is our recommended default for most private deployments; TLS can terminate at the customer edge (recommended) or at a customer-managed ingress proxy in the customer VPC; audit telemetry can be scoped such that sensitive token content is never sent to Redwood's control plane (we can provide aggregated/masked traces).

I've attached a first-pass reference diagram (e2e-traffic-flow-v1.svg) and a control/data ownership matrix (control-data-ownership-matrix.xlsx) — both are intentionally conservative and call out where customer-managed components are required for compliance. Please review.

Open questions we want to resolve in the workshop:
- Does Helios require KMS keys to be customer-held (HSM/KMS) for inference session metadata?
- Any mandatory egress-only firewall controls (TLS interception policies) beyond standard outbound allowlist?
- Requirements around audit retention and export format (Syslog vs S3 archives).

Proposed times for a 60-minute workshop: Dec 18 10:00-11:00 PT or Dec 20 09:00-10:00 PT. Which works for your security and infra leads?

Next steps if you confirm time: Jonas and Irene will join to walk the diagram and note any operational constraints.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
(650) 555-0199

Attachments: e2e-traffic-flow-v1.svg (diagram), control-data-ownership-matrix.xlsx (ownership matrix)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial: private VPC boundary & e2e traffic flow

Folks — quick internal alignment before we run the workshop with Helios. Notes on the diagram and proposed stance:

1) Outbound-only model: agree as default. We'll publish a hardened egress endpoint list (regional) and a short-lived client cert model for session establishment.
2) TLS termination: prefer customer-edge termination. If customer asks Redwood to terminate, require a customer-provided cert and explicit KMS escrow policy documented in the contract.
3) Control plane responsibilities: provisioning, metric aggregation, scheduling, and rollback/rollout orchestration. Data plane responsibilities: model runtime, KV cache, and inference traffic — belongs to customer VPC in private deploy.
4) HA/DR patterns: propose active/active inference nodes in two AZs within customer VPC + control plane in two Redwood regions behind edge relays.

I attached an updated diagram with a proposed edge-relay pattern and a clearer demarcation for control vs data flows (e2e-traffic-flow-v2.svg). Action items:
- Irene: add notes on telemetry masking and minimum retention (SOC2)
- Ben: surface the contract language needed if Redwood will hold any crypto on behalf of customer
- Evelyn: confirm workshop cadence and send invites.

Jonas
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachments: e2e-traffic-flow-v2.svg
From: Sarah Murphy <sarah.murphy@heliosfi.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Helios Solutions Architect <solutions@heliosfi.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 08:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial: private VPC boundary & e2e traffic flow

Evelyn/Jonas — thanks for the speed here. A few clarifications from our security team after looking at v2: 

- We will require TLS termination at our edge. Redwood should accept mTLS from an outbound connection initiated by our proxy; Redwood must not request inbound connections.
- KMS: Helios policy requires customer-managed KMS keys for encryption of inference session metadata. We are open to Redwood integrating with our KMS via a customer-provided role and kms:Encrypt/Decrypt permissions.
- Telemetry: fine with aggregated metrics only. We will provide an S3 bucket for audit log export (AES-256 SSE). Retention policy: 7 years for specific audit events.

We can take Dec 20 09:00-10:00 PT for the workshop. I'll invite our infra and security leads and share a short pre-read (design doc link below).

Pre-read: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cDesignDoc

Regards,
Sarah

Thanks all — workshop confirmed for Dec 20 09:00 PT. Final pre-work and immediate action items: 

1) Helios (Sarah): share the S3 bucket write policy and the KMS key ARN so we can validate cross-account permissions pre-workshop.
2) Redwood (Irene): prepare a short slide that shows telemetry masking rules + minimal event schema we will export to S3. Link it in the meeting notes.
3) Redwood (Ben): draft contract language for customer-managed KMS and for any case where Redwood holds ephemeral crypto (we will prefer not to).
4) Jonas & Monica: be ready to walk the updated e2e-traffic-flow-v2.svg and a one-page deploy playbook (deploy-playbook-actions.docx).

I attached the deploy playbook stub for review. We'll record the session and follow up with a definitive demarcation diagram and a checklist for the onboarding runbook.

See you on the 20th.

Best,
